title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is handwritten on the verso of a Bourbaki typescript draft (n°370, Haar measure, existence theorem). The neighbouring pages are that typescript, not Grothendieck's own notes, so the page has no mathematical context of his own around it. The hand is very hard to read and much of it is struck through. What can be made out, read conservatively:

(1) Grothendieck recalls something said 'plus haut' (earlier in the notes): an object, almost certainly a motive or a family of motives over an arithmetic base, is 'très loin d'être caractérisé par les fonctions L correspondantes' when these are viewed as functions of a point of a moduli space ('fonctions de la [variété?] modulaire').

(2) He then asks: 'Mais que se passe-t-il si on les regarde comme fonctions des structures de Hodge ?' That is, replace the arithmetic invariant (L-functions, pointwise in the parameter) by the Hodge-theoretic one (the variation of Hodge structure over the base).

(3) He states that something is 'vrai pour une relation H-locale(?)'. This plausibly means a relation that holds Hodge-theoretically locally, i.e. a Hodge class that is flat or locally constant in the family.

(4) He sketches a chain of reductions, standard dévissage style:
- k_0 := the algebraic closure of Q in k (the diagram Q – k_0 – k, X in the margin);
- X of finite type over Q (spreading out);
- X a curve of finite type over C (curves through points);
- possibly birational reductions (struck out: 'ramené au cas X = P^1_C').

(5) Final conclusion: 'Il semble suffire de vérifier … au cas où X = P^1_C − (0) − (1) − (∞), et donc sur Q̄'. This is where the theory reduces to data 'équivalente comme [?]' to that defined by a motivic relation over X, with some invariant of indeterminacy.

In modern language this reads as a principle-B type argument: a Hodge-type relation (a Hodge class or 'relation motivée') in a family over a connected base X, if motivic or absolute at one fibre, is so at all fibres. Spreading out and cutting by curves reduces the general statement to a universal base.

The striking step is the reduction of an arbitrary curve to the thrice-punctured line, with the added 'et donc sur Q̄'. For curves over Q̄ this would follow from Belyi's theorem (1979): an open subset of the curve is finite étale over P^1 − {0,1,∞}. That is presumably why the descent to Q̄ is needed. No justification for the step is written on the page.
errors: The reduction from an arbitrary curve of finite type over C to P^1 − {0,1,∞} cannot work over C as such: a curve with transcendental moduli is not finite étale over an open of P^1 − {0,1,∞}. Grothendieck's added 'et donc sur Q̄' partly acknowledges this. Even over Q̄, the step needs Belyi's theorem (or an equivalent), which is not given on the page.

The steps are indicated, not proved. Several are struck through, and the exact statement being reduced (what 'relation H-locale' and the final 'invariant d'indétermination' mean) is not recoverable with certainty.

ideas.what: Motives (or families of motives) are far from determined by their L-functions viewed pointwise over a moduli space; one should instead use the variation of Hodge structure.
ideas.modern_name: Hodge realization versus L-function realization; conservativity of realizations; variations of Hodge structure as invariants of families of motives
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck and Serre (motivic philosophy); Deligne (Hodge II, 1971)
ideas.where_published: Ideas of this type appear in Grothendieck–Serre correspondence and in Récoltes et Semailles discussions of motives; not this specific remark

ideas.what: A relation that holds Hodge-theoretically locally (flat Hodge class) propagates over a connected base. Reduction: k_0 = alg. closure of Q in k, then X of finite type over Q, then curves over C.
ideas.modern_name: Deligne's Principle B for absolute Hodge cycles; André's motivated cycles; spreading-out dévissage
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Hodge cycles on abelian varieties, 1982); Y. André (1996)

ideas.what: Reduction of the problem for curves to the universal case X = P^1 − {0,1,∞}, 'et donc sur Q̄'.
ideas.modern_name: Belyi-type reduction (every curve over Q̄ has an open finite étale over P^1 − {0,1,∞}); anabelian / dessins philosophy
ideas.usually_credited_to: G. V. Belyi (1979); Grothendieck, Esquisse d'un programme (1984)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) emphasizes P^1 − {0,1,∞} and Belyi's theorem; this application to Hodge/motivic relations is not there

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches a strategy to prove a statement about motivic relations in families via Hodge theory. It reduces, by spreading out and cutting by curves, to a single universal base P^1 − {0,1,∞} over Q̄. This is a principle-B-style argument with a Belyi-type final reduction. It is an early, undated anticipation of Deligne's absolute-Hodge reduction strategy, combined with the special role of the thrice-punctured line.
missed.quote: Il semble suffire de vérifier ... au cas où X = P^1_C − (0) − (1) − (∞), et donc sur Q̄
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: If datable to before 1979, it would show Grothendieck already viewing P^1 − {0,1,∞} as a universal test case for motivic or Hodge questions over Q̄, predating Belyi. Reducing motivic and Hodge questions on families to the thrice-punctured line, e.g. via mixed Tate and hypergeometric motives over it, is not a standard route in the literature on absolute Hodge or motivated cycles.

missed.claim: An implicit link between the L-function versus Hodge-structure characterization of families of motives and the anabelian, P^1 − {0,1,∞} reduction.
missed.quote: Mais que se passe-t-il si on les regarde comme fonctions des structures de Hodge ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It connects conservativity of realizations for families with Belyi-type reductions, a combination not usually made explicit.

deep.surprise_reason: The reading is very uncertain, but the page appears to sketch a principle-B-type reduction of a Hodge/motivic statement to P^1 − {0,1,∞} over Q̄. If the dating (1965 to circa 1977) precedes Belyi (1979), this is a notable unpublished anticipation. The illegibility and lack of a stated proof keep the score moderate.
transcription_corrections: Line 2 likely reads 'plus [?] est très loin d'être caractérisé par les fonctions L correspondantes', with 'motif' (or family of motives) as the probable subject.
'fonctions des [?] structures de Hodge' is probably 'fonctions des (variations de) structures de Hodge'; the struck word may be 'variations' or 'directement'.
'Vrai pour une relation H local' plausibly 'relation H-locale' or 'relation de Hodge locale'.
The X-is-a-curve line probably reads 'au cas où X est courbe de type fini sur C'.
The interlinear addition after P^1 − (0) − (1) − (∞) reads roughly 'et donc sur Q̄ (et donc sur Q̄ ... Gal.)'; the descent to Q̄ is explicit.
The final lines likely contain 'relation motivique(?) sur X, d'invariant ... d'indétermination'; the bracket closes at 'indétermination ]'.
The page number at bottom left is 224.
